exploration.title: Leaf Energy Lab
exploration.subject: Biology
exploration.summary: Adjust light and water to investigate what limits a leaf’s sugar-making process.
exploration.question: Can more sunlight help when a plant has too little water?
exploration.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to convert water and carbon dioxide into sugars, releasing oxygen. A shortage of a needed resource can limit the process; more light does not guarantee proportionally more activity. This qualitative resource model is not a growth forecast and leaves out temperature, species differences and many other processes. Plants also respire, by day and night.

experiments.title: Test a missing resource
experiments.instruction: Predict whether extra light can restore activity when water is absent. Choose a prediction, then Test zero water and extra light. Keep carbon dioxide fixed.
experiments.observe: Activity remains zero. Explain why light cannot replace water in sugar production.

experiments.title: Find the limiting resource
experiments.instruction: Reset experiment, Save comparison, then predict what raising water above 80% will do while light 70% and carbon dioxide 80% remain fixed. Raise only water.
experiments.observe: Activity first rises, then light becomes limiting. Compare the saved trial and explain why more water cannot replace light.

exploration.misconception: Plants make sugars; they do not absorb their sugar food from soil. Soil supplies water and mineral nutrients, and sunlight supplies energy rather than matter.
